VERDICT: FAIL

Independent audit of P1 against the phase-scoped catalogue and plan. High findings include incorrect seeded bookings and tests that claim coverage they do not provide. The audit regressions are intentionally failing; no product code or existing tests were changed.

| Severity | Location | Scenario and evidence | Minimal fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High | `src/labquorum/store/seed.py:56`, `seed/demo.yaml:114`, `tests/integration/test_p1_ledger.py:275` | The seed treats the recording anchor as the booking day, even when closed. With Sunday 2026-11-08 as anchor, BK-0041 starts `2026-11-08T08:30:00Z`, not Monday 2026-11-09 14:00 IST. The plan specifies the next open day after recording (`docs/plan/templates/seed-data.md:5`, `:28`); the I-10 test instead asserts the anchor itself, so it passes the incorrect behavior. Friday anchors also book Friday rather than the following open day. Reproduced by `test_seed_bookings_fall_on_next_open_day`. | Derive the next open date strictly after the anchor using the instrument schedule, preserve idempotency, and test Friday and Sunday anchors with the resulting demo alternative. |

If that predicate misses gap-only conflicts, both properties can pass while violating the invariant. U-B02 uses a direct overlap, so it also cannot detect an omitted gap. ## Scope and observations

- The booking predicate in `src/labquorum/domain/booking.py:92` matches the specified strict half-open gap expression. `commit_booking` rechecks committed bookings under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before updating the proposed booking. Only committed bookings occupy a slot, matching `docs/plan/03-architecture.md:154`; proposals may overlap and are rechecked at commit. I-01 uses spawned OS processes, a barrier before commit, 50 pairs and a real unsafe read-before-lock probe. I-25 uses five spawned writers. These checks do not remedy the shared-oracle property weakness above; no actual double booking was demonstrated.
- Pending commits compare the incoming canonical decision bytes and supplied revision/hash with stored values and recompute the stored decision hash. Expiry is inclusive, revisions invalidate earlier decisions, and repeated matching commits return the stored booking without another audit event. Decline and expiry are checked in the repository, subject to the P-05 coverage gap above. The committed retry branch does not recompute the hash, but no ordinary operation changes its stored decision.
- Canonical JSON sorts keys, emits Unicode and rejects floats. The cap counts Python characters of the compact serialized decision; the exact boundary defect is above. Zone parsing refuses local gaps and folds and accepts explicit offsets; `tzdata` is declared. U-B10 covers the two New York folds. Clock grep found `datetime.now` only in `SystemClock` and no `time.time` in `src`.
- The audit hash includes sequence, timestamp, actor, tool, arguments, result and previous hash; verification checks continuity and hashes. An internally recomputed chain and a truncated suffix are inherently undetectable without an external checkpoint. The existing suite does not exercise middle insertion/deletion; this is a coverage observation, not a claim that verification fails them.
- The seed has the specified Lena 14:00-15:30 booking and 15-minute gap, and the pure nearest-slot example returns 15:45-16:45 on the test's Friday. The incorrect anchor handling prevents this being a reliable recording-day fixture. Repeated same-anchor seeding is tested for idempotency.
- SQL values inspected are parameterized; the interpolated PRAGMA values are internal constants or an internally selected allowlist. No `type: ignore` or pyright ignore was found in `src`. Connection ownership is generally explicit, though exceptional setup failures in `init_database` and `_connect` can leave connections open. Broad exception handling was not found in product paths. Deferred P2 MCP and runtime card certification were not evaluated as P1 implementation.
- `git diff 63f7c78 HEAD -- tests` showed no changes to the original named P1 test files; the fixture diff consists of annotations, and the documented post-red error-path file adds tests. The red commit also includes stubs and seed data. I did not independently run the historical red commit, so its claimed behavioral-red execution remains UNVERIFIED in this audit. No post-red deletion or weakening of the original assertions was found.

## Executed checks

- Before audit regressions: `uv run pytest -q` passed, 56 passed in 31.65s.
- `uv run pytest -q tests/audit/test_p1_boundaries.py` failed as intended: 3 failed, with the three concrete findings above.
- After adding the regressions, `uv run pytest -q` failed as expected: 3 failed, 56 passed in 32.39s. `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, and `uv run pyright` passed after correcting audit-test imports.
- The claimed gate pass was supplied by the orchestrator; it was not rerun by this auditor. Windows was the only platform exercised here; Ubuntu behavior and live Switch certification are UNVERIFIED.
